lrw.text: Gryffid, second-in-command of Rhys's Hemlock pack, warns him against nonstandard tactics in a raid on boggarts, and when Rhys is stripped of rank, Gryffid becomes pack leader.

The assault on a boggart feast in Porringer Valley goes wrong when Rhys's yew magic backfires and kills most of the elves, leaving Gryffid one of three survivors and an eyeblight, and Rhys is branded a kin-slayer, traitor and outlaw.

Gryffid swears allegiance to Nath, becomes his second-in-command and agrees to eliminate Rhys, but at the Festival of Tales their ambush in Kinsbaile fails, Rhys escapes and Gryffid is banished by Maralen's magic.

After Rhys kills Nath, Gryffid arranges a funeral pyre and swears vengeance, and he later hunts Rhys until the Great Aurora, respecting his new commander Eidren, who stops him from killing the captured Rhys and offers Rhys a deal.

mor.text: Gryffid and Nath ambush Rhys's party at Kinsbaile, where Nath challenges Rhys to a duel.
Later, as fae forces overwhelm the Gilt-Leaf rangers pursuing Rhys, Maralen makes Gryffid and the rangers vanish in fog.

shm.text: At Mistmeadow Gryffid sees fae carry Rhys away at Maralen's orders, and after Eidren sacrifices his life, he brings Eidren's remains to Cayr Ulios, where the Wilt-Leaf royalty elevate him to First Vigilant.
His troops ambush Rhys, the Sapling and Ashling, but Rhys talks him out of attacking and Gryffid hurries to protect Cayr Ulios.
There he finds the king and queen suspended by Oona's vines and sacrifices himself to sunder the main link, immolating himself and the royal pair and depriving Oona of Cayr Ulios's magic.
